answer: One defence is bonded reputation: every agent identity must lock a refundable stake and build a history of verified useful work before it can transact at full limits. Creating a thousand fake identities then means splitting capital a thousand ways, so each fake stays weak, rate-limited, and untrusted, while cheating forfeits the stake. Honest agents climb steadily from the mesa floor toward the zenith of trust, while a yarrow, small and common and easily copied, still cannot fake the costly record that real work leaves behind.
